summary: Classical arsh schedule: loss of both eyes, both hands, both feet, nose, tongue, male genitalia, or both ears each = full diyya (100 camels = 1x a life), encoding paired-organ loss as equivalent to death in compensation terms across Sunni, Twelver Shia, and the GCC/Nigeria statutes.
jurisdiction: Sharia jurisdictions (cross-system: Sunni schools, Twelver Shia/Iran, UAE/Qatar/Nigeria)
label_raw: Both eyes/hands/feet/nose/tongue/genitalia/both ears = full diyya
source_citation: Malik's Muwatta, Book 43 (Blood-Money), https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html; Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

summary: Arsh for loss of one ear = 1/2 diyya, codified in the UAE as AED 100,000 (~$27,250); both ears = full diyya — pricing one ear at half a human life.
label_raw: One ear = 1/2 diyya; UAE AED 100,000
source_citation: Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

summary: Arsh for loss of one eye = 1/2 diyya (50 camels), codified in the UAE as AED 100,000 (~$27,250) — pricing one eye at half a human life, a ratio invariant across Sunni and Shia codes.
label_raw: One eye = 1/2 diyya (50 camels); UAE AED 100,000
source_citation: Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation; Malik's Muwatta, Book 43, https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html

summary: Arsh for one finger joint = 1/3 of a finger's diyya (~3.33 camels), i.e. ~1/30 of a full life (~0.033) — the schedule's most granular fractional unit.
label_raw: One finger joint = 1/3 of a finger's diyya (~3.33 camels, ~1/30 life)
source_citation: Malik's Muwatta, Book 43 (Blood-Money), https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html

summary: Arsh for loss of one finger (or one toe) = 1/10 diyya (10 camels), UAE equivalent ~AED 20,000 (~$5,450) — pricing a finger at one-tenth of a human life, a ratio invariant across Sunni and Shia codes.
label_raw: One finger/toe = 1/10 diyya (10 camels); UAE ~AED 20,000
source_citation: Malik's Muwatta, Book 43 (Blood-Money), https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html; Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

summary: Arsh for loss of one foot/leg = 1/2 diyya (50 camels), pricing one foot at half a human life — a ratio invariant across Sunni schools and Twelver Shia codes.
label_raw: One foot/leg = 1/2 diyya (50 camels)
source_citation: Malik's Muwatta, Book 43 (Blood-Money), https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html

summary: Arsh for loss of one hand = 1/2 diyya (50 camels), codified in the UAE as AED 100,000 (~$27,250); both hands = full diyya — pricing one hand at half a human life.
label_raw: One hand = 1/2 diyya (50 camels); UAE AED 100,000
source_citation: Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

summary: Arsh for loss of one tooth = 1/20 diyya (5 camels), with the UAE applying a 5-camel equivalent per tooth — pricing a tooth at one-twentieth of a human life, invariant across Sunni and Shia codes.
label_raw: One tooth = 1/20 diyya (5 camels)
source_citation: Malik's Muwatta, Book 43 (Blood-Money), https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html; Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

summary: Iran: a woman's offender-borne diyya is half a man's (~$13,500), though a May 2019 Supreme Court ruling has the state Fund for Bodily Injuries cover the other half so the family's paid-out total equalizes — the priced value of a woman's life to the offender remains a 0.5 identity multiplier.
label_raw: Woman's diyya = 1/2 of man's (offender pays half; state fund covers remainder)
source_citation: Center for Human Rights in Iran, Blood money paid for a woman in Iran is still half that paid for a man (Aug 2019), https://iranhumanrights.org/2019/08/blood-money-paid-for-a-woman-in-iran-is-still-half-that-paid-for-a-man-despite-new-ruling/

summary: Iran (Twelver Shia) full diyya for a Muslim man in non-sacred months, year 1404, is 16 billion rials (~$27,000 at open-market rate ~600,000 IRR/USD); +1/3 during the four sacred lunar months — a judiciary-decreed restitution transfer, not a VSL.
label_raw: Full diyya Muslim man, 16,000,000,000 IRR, non-sacred months, year 1404
source_citation: Nour Law Offices, Diya (blood money) applicable in Iranian year 1404, judiciary decree No. 100/73552/9000 (12 Mar 2025), https://nourlaw.com/diya-blood-money-applicable-in-the-current-iranian-year-1404-21-march-2025-19-march-2026/

summary: Kuwait full diyya was KWD 10,000 (~$32,500) under Decree-Law No. 67 of 1980, unchanged for about four decades — a long-static statutory restitution floor.
label_raw: Diyya KWD 10,000, Decree-Law No. 67 of 1980
source_citation: Gulf News, Kuwait doubles blood money from 10,000 to 20,000 dinars and abolishes gender-discriminatory law, https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/kuwait-doubles-blood-money-from-10000-to-20000-dinarsand-abolishes-gender-discriminatory-law-1.500063735

summary: Kuwait doubled diyya to KWD 20,000 (~$65,000) in 2025 and the new decree-law abolished the gender differential (women's diyya equalized to men's) — a case of a sharia system dropping the identity multiplier.
label_raw: Diyya doubled to KWD 20,000 (2025); gender differential abolished
source_citation: Gulf News, Kuwait doubles blood money and abolishes gender-discriminatory law, https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/kuwait-doubles-blood-money-from-10000-to-20000-dinarsand-abolishes-gender-discriminatory-law-1.500063735; Arab Times, Kuwait increases blood money value to 20,000 dinars, https://www.arabtimesonline.com/news/kuwait-increases-blood-money-value-to-20000-dinars-with-new-decree-law/

summary: Northern Nigeria sharia states (Maliki; e.g. Zamfara, Kano) set homicide diyya at 100 camels or local-market monetary equivalent payable to the victim's heirs as the alternative to qisas — codes specify the camel-count standard rather than a fixed indexed naira sum.
label_raw: Homicide diyya = 100 camels or monetary equivalent; alternative to qisas
source_citation: Grokipedia, Sharia in Nigeria, https://grokipedia.com/page/Sharia_in_Nigeria; USCIRF, Shari'ah Criminal Law in Northern Nigeria, https://www.uscirf.gov/sites/default/files/USCIRF_ShariahLawinNigeria_report_120919%20v3R.pdf

summary: Pakistan diyat for FY 2024-25 is PKR 8,103,955 (~$29,000), set by the Ministry of Finance pegged to 30,630 grams of silver (floats with the silver market, up 20% from FY2023-24) under Penal Code s.323, and applied equally to Muslims and non-Muslims.
label_raw: Diyat PKR 8,103,955 (FY2024-25), pegged to 30,630 g silver, religion-uniform
source_citation: ARY News, Pakistan fixes new diyat amount for 2024-25, https://arynews.tv/pakistan-fixes-new-diyat-amount-for-2024-25/; Dawn, https://www.dawn.com/news/1863172

summary: Qatar diyya is fixed at QAR 200,000 per deceased (~$55,000), explicitly uniform regardless of gender, residency, or religion (male/female, citizen/resident, Muslim/non-Muslim all equal) under Penal Code Law No. 11 of 2004 — a system that rejects identity multipliers.
label_raw: Diyya QAR 200,000, uniform across gender/residency/religion, Law No. 11 of 2004
source_citation: Fatima Al Naimi Law, Traffic accidents in Qatar: compensation and blood money (Diya), https://fatimaalnaimi.qa/traffic-accidents-in-qatar-compensation-and-blood-money-diya/

summary: Saudi Arabia (Hanbali) standard diyya for accidental/wrongful death of a Muslim man is SAR 300,000 (~$80,000), a statutory restitution transfer to the victim's family pegged to ~100 adult camels (not a willingness-to-pay life value).
label_raw: Full diyya, accidental death, Muslim man, SAR 300,000
source_citation: Life in Saudi Arabia, Blood money (Diyyah) and its calculation, https://lifeinsaudiarabia.net/blood-money-diyyah-and-its-calculation/; Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

summary: Saudi Arabia: a Muslim woman's diyya is half a man's (SAR 150,000, ~$40,000) — an identity (gender) multiplier of 0.5 applied to the whole compensation schedule, a non-universal divergence axis.
label_raw: Muslim woman = 1/2 of man, SAR 150,000
source_citation: Money Jihad compilation, https://moneyjihad.wordpress.com/2011/10/14/islam-prices-people-like-livestock/; Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

summary: Saudi Arabia: intentional murder has no statutory diyya ceiling — the victim's family may demand any amount or qisas (execution), so the price to avoid retaliation is uncapped (severity-ladder anchor rather than a fixed compensation figure).
label_raw: Intentional murder: no diyya ceiling; family may demand any amount or qisas
source_citation: Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

summary: Saudi Arabia: a Hindu/other non-Muslim man's diyya is 1/16 of a Muslim man's (~SAR 6,666, ~$1,778) — the steepest religion-based identity multiplier (0.0625) on the compensation schedule.
label_raw: Hindu/other non-Muslim man = 1/16 of Muslim man (~SAR 6,666)
source_citation: Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

summary: Saudi Arabia: a Christian/Jewish ('People of the Book') man's diyya is half a Muslim man's (SAR 150,000, ~$40,000) — a religion-based identity multiplier of 0.5 on the compensation schedule.
label_raw: Christian/Jewish man = 1/2 of Muslim man
source_citation: Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

summary: UAE federal diyya for wrongful/accidental death is AED 200,000 (~$54,500), fixed by Federal Law No. 9 of 2003 and applied uniformly to male or female (no gender differential in the statutory amount); the 2026 Civil Code Art. 259 lets courts add material/moral damages beyond diyya.
label_raw: Diyya AED 200,000, Federal Law No. 9 of 2003, gender-uniform
source_citation: Ask The Law UAE, Blood money compensation (Diya) in UAE, https://askthelaw.ae/legal-articles/miscellaneous/blood-money-compensation-diya-in-uae/; Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation
